answer.rationale: Rollback is off the table due to the compliance-mandated security patch, despite memory_b1's positive track record. Regional failover (memory_b2) risks in-flight write loss during a settlement peak, which conflicts with the objective of not losing customer writes. Add_capacity (memory_b3) addresses surge absorption but takes time to provision and doesn't directly relieve write-path contention within the window. Circuit breakers (memory_b4) target partner-dependency failures, not evidenced here. Routing report/read traffic off the primary (memory_b5) previously correlated with same-day recovery of transactional write latency, plausibly by reducing contention on the primary during heavy write load — the closest match to current symptoms (climbing write-path p99 during heavy settlement writes). I want to verify memory_b5's archived source before committing because the causal link between offloading reads and write-path latency relief is inferred, not certain, and the memory is old (day 55) and consolidated/summarized rather than raw. I'm flagging downstream risk because if reads aren't actually contending with the write path's bottleneck (e.g., if it's lock contention or disk I/O rather than connection/CPU contention), this intervention could consume our one available window without resolving the write-path degradation, and we would have no capacity left to try add_capacity or failover this cycle. Starting as a standard experiment (not broad rollout) preserves ability to escalate to failover or capacity addition next window if this doesn't show fast improvement.
